statement: Day-10 closure of the EOG physical-burden blocker for the CURRENT Sleep-EDF 5-class sleep-stage use case, as far as defensible engineering evidence permits. This models the incremental contact/module burden of adding one horizontal-EOG channel to the existing frontal-EEG head module. It does NOT invent a final consumer product, does NOT freeze exact electrode geometry beyond what the signal requires, and does NOT assert system power or system mass. Unknowns remain unknown.

scope.dataset_context: Sleep-EDF (EEG Fpz-Cz baseline; EOG horizontal candidate; both real, same 100 Hz sample rate)

signal_requirement.experiment_channel_identity: "EOG horizontal" (Sleep-EDF PSG), single differential channel at 100 Hz
signal_requirement.note: The frozen sleep experiment used exactly one horizontal-EOG channel added to the single EEG Fpz-Cz derivation. Vertical EOG, multi-channel oculography, or a full clinical montage are NOT required by the current result and are not modeled here.

physical_site.placement: lateral to the outer canthi (bilateral), the standard horizontal-EOG placement
physical_site.relationship_to_existing_head_module: adjacent to the forehead/frontal-EEG region; a new physical sensing SITE, but not obviously a new distant body region
physical_site.new_body_region_status: AMBIGUOUS_ADJACENT — peri-ocular is contiguous with the existing forehead head-module region; whether it counts as a distinct 'new region' or an extension of the head region is a framing choice, left explicit rather than forced to zero or to one.

contact_burden_interpretations.note: The exact incremental electrode/contact count depends on whether the EOG reference and bias/DRL are shared with the existing EEG head module. Both interpretations are modeled; neither is collapsed into a single 'EOG = 2 electrodes' headline.

standalone_incremental_interpretation.assumption: EOG measured as a fully independent front-end (its own reference and bias/DRL network, no sharing with EEG).
standalone_incremental_interpretation.total_incremental_contacts_range: 3-4 (3 if a single electrode serves combined reference/bias; 4 if reference and bias/DRL are separate)
standalone_incremental_interpretation.module_impact: Plausibly a new or clearly-separable front-end; a standalone EOG channel that does not reuse the EEG reference network is closer to an independent acquisition path.

shared_reference_architecture_interpreta.assumption: EOG shares the reference (SRB) and bias-drive (BIASOUT) network of the existing ADS1299-4-class frontal-EEG head module, and is wired into a spare channel of that same AFE.
shared_reference_architecture_interpreta.afe_channel_headroom: The ADS1299-4 class is a 4-channel biopotential AFE; the current reference EEG uses a single Fpz-Cz derivation, so at least one spare channel is available for the one EOG differential channel without adding a second AFE. This is an architectural-count observation, not a validated final montage.
shared_reference_architecture_interpreta.shared_reference_basis: ADS1299-family devices provide a common bias-drive (BIASOUT) and reference-select (SRB) network shared across all channels by design; a co-located ocular channel on the same head module can reuse it. Datasheet-class capability, not a frozen wiring diagram.
shared_reference_architecture_interpreta.module_impact: No new hardware module: the EOG channel is wired to the existing head-module AFE. Head attachment extends to the peri-ocular sites.

burden_output.physical_region_increment: 0 or 1 (peri-ocular is contiguous with the head region; framing-dependent, not forced)
burden_output.module_increment: 0 in the shared-reference interpretation (wired to existing head module); potentially 1 in the standalone interpretation
burden_output.sensing_contact_increment: 2 (both interpretations agree the horizontal-EOG channel needs 2 lateral-ocular sensing electrodes)
burden_output.reference_bias_contact_increment: 0 if reference/bias shared with EEG head module; up to 2 if standalone
burden_output.attachment_increment: extend the existing head attachment to the peri-ocular sites (2 additional electrode positions); no new independent strap/harness required in the shared interpretation
burden_output.wiring_increment: 2 electrode leads routed to the head-module AFE (shared interpretation)

compute_increment.basis: EEG-only classifier 8,197 params -> EEG+EOG classifier 8,309 params = +112 (the constant per-channel convention verified in the interaction experiment).
compute_increment.note: Model/compute increment only; not an embedded latency or energy measurement.

data_rate_increment.basis: 1 channel x 100 Hz x 24-bit ADS1299-class conversion. Excludes framing, protocol, and transport overhead.
data_rate_increment.note: Scientific-reference payload rate; the Sleep-EDF EOG horizontal channel is 100 Hz.

burden_output.power_increment_note: One additional biopotential channel on the shared (already-counted) ADS1299-class head-module AFE. No standalone EOG operating point, session duty cycle, or complete head-module power state is frozen, so no incremental average power is asserted. Not zero, not quantified.
burden_output.mass_increment_note: Two additional ocular electrodes plus leads. Electrode material/adhesive, lead mass, and any peri-ocular attachment mechanics are not selected. Component/PCB/enclosure mass for the head module remains unresolved upstream. Not zero, not quantified.
burden_output.uncertainty: The dominant uncertainty is the standalone-vs-shared-reference wiring (which drives whether the contact increment is 2 or up to 4 and whether a new module is added), plus fully-unquantified incremental power and mass. The sensing-contact increment of 2 is the one interpretation-independent, defensible quantity.

comparison_to_imu_burden.note: For gate calibration only. The wrist-IMU CONDITIONAL case has near-zero incremental HUMAN contact burden (colocated inside the existing wrist enclosure, 0 new electrodes/region). EOG's incremental burden is materially higher: at least 2 new ocular sensing electrodes and a new peri-ocular sensing site, even in the most favorable shared-reference interpretation. This is why EOG remains CONDITIONAL rather than upgrading, despite strong within-dataset science.

unresolved_items: Exact standalone vs shared-reference wiring is not frozen (both modeled).
Whether peri-ocular counts as a distinct new body region or a head-region extension is a framing choice, left explicit.
Incremental average power and daily energy (session schedule/operating point open).
Incremental finished mass (electrode/adhesive/lead/attachment materials not selected).
Long-term ocular-electrode wearability, skin tolerance, and motion robustness in the intended setting.
Whether a single reference electrode can serve both EEG and EOG at acceptable signal quality (assumed plausible, not validated).
closure_rationale: The contact/module/wiring/compute/data-rate increments are now defensibly modeled under two explicit reference interpretations (standalone and shared-reference), replacing the prior 'MISSING/UNRESOLVED, contact burden unknown' state. The sensing-contact increment (2) is defensible and interpretation-independent; the shared-reference path plausibly needs no new module and no new reference/bias contacts. Power and mass remain honestly NOT_READY. This closes the qualitative structure of the EOG burden while preserving the quantitative unknowns.
prohibited_upgrades: Do not treat the EOG contact/electrode burden as zero.
Do not assert an exact final electrode geometry beyond the signal-required 2 sensing electrodes.
Do not assert incremental EOG system power or system mass.
Do not use this burden closure to upgrade EOG from CONDITIONAL_FOR_TARGET to RETAIN.
